2609.28060.title: A Native-Reference Coordinate Geometry for L2 Pronunciation Deviation Using Self-Supervised Speech Models
2609.28060.paper_summary: Self-supervised speech models encode rich phonetic information, but it remains unclear how to transform this information into interpretable metrics for second-language (L2) pronunciation assessment in spontaneous speech. We propose a native-reference coordinate geometry in which phone-class averages from native speech define a low-dimensional reference subspace, and L2 speech is evaluated by its distance to matching native phone-class coordinates. Unlike prior distance-based approaches, our method does not require parallel recordings with matched linguistic content or dedicated pronunciation labels. Across different self-supervised encoders and modeling choices, the resulting native-reference distances show negative Spearman correlations up to -0.5 with speaking proficiency, indicating that higher-proficiency speakers tend to lie closer to the native-reference space.
2609.28060.paper_summary_zh: 自我監督的語音模型編碼了豐富的語音信息，但如何將這些信息轉化為可解釋的指標以評估自發語言的第二語言 (L2) 發音仍然不清楚。<lb/>我們提出了一種以母語參考為基礎的坐標幾何，其中來自母語的音素類平均值定義了一個低維的參考子空間，而 L2 語音則通過其與匹配的母語音素類坐標的距離來進行評估。<lb/>與先前基於距離的方法不同，我們的方法不需要具有匹配語言內容的平行錄音或專門的發音標籤。<lb/>在不同的自我監督編碼器和建模選擇中，所得到的母語參考距離與口語熟練度之間顯示出高達 -0.5 的負斯皮爾曼相關性，這表明更高熟練度的說話者往往更接近母語參考空間。
